items.title: Nvidia stock falls amid probe into CEO’s relationship with Chinese spy
items.summary:
By Steve Kopack and Rob Wile

Nvidia’s stock slid about 4% on Monday after the company announced that it had opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman that U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.

The probe has the potential to unsettle the entire AI boom, fueled by trillions of dollars of spending and investments, in part to purchase Nvidia’s cutting-edge AI chips. Nvidia’s drop wiped out more than $200 billion in value. [...] Nvidia’s peers, such as AMD, Qualcomm, Taiwan Semi and Intel, all rose along with the broader market. Nvidia was the biggest loser on the Dow, the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500.

With so many outstanding questions about the Huang scandal, few major analysts that cover Nvidia had weighed in on Monday morning about what it could mean for the company’s future.

But those who did said it was a blemish on an otherwise sterling track record, which could spark even more investigations. [...] “A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation,” Nvidia said in a Sunday statement. “The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.”

An Nvidia spokesperson told NBC News that Huang was “committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.”

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang delivers his keynote on the company's GTC event in Berlin, Germany, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026.  Markus Schreiber/AP  hide caption

 Markus Schreiber/AP

The massive artificial intelligence chip maker Nvidia says it is launching an internal investigation, after reports that the company's CEO was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. [...] Nvidia dominates the global market for AI chips, and has seen explosive growth in recent years, as NPR has reported. The company started as a manufacturer of chips for computer graphics, which later turned out to be crucial for training artificial intelligence.

Nvidia's CEO and President Trump have repeatedly appeared in public together in recent years. According to Huang, Nvidia is helping to fund the construction of a new ballroom at the White House. [...] In the statement announcing the investigation, Nvidia cited recent reporting by The New York Times, which alleges Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation that sought to send advanced Nvidia AI chips to China.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the statement from the company's board of directors reads in part.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits affair, board to launch investigation
items.summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy in a message to his company, and the company's board announced an independent investigation Sunday.

Why it matters:The scandal raises national security concerns involving one of the world's most powerful tech CEOs, who has pushed to loosen restrictions on selling advanced AI chips to China amid the two countries' race for technological dominance. [...] "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did."
   Huang said he took "full responsibility" for his actions, adding that he had fallen short of his responsibilities to Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders.
   "Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life," Huang wrote. "I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."
